DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Fibroma (Meigs' Syndrome).

The combination of a benign-appearing ovarian mass, ascites, and a right-sided pleural effusion (spontaneous pneumothorax is also a known complication, though less likely without trauma) in a patient with a normal CA-125 is highly characteristic of Meigs' syndrome. The normal CA-125 helps rule out epithelial ovarian carcinoma, which typically presents with elevated markers in this context. I will confirm the final diagnosis once the histology is available, but clinically, this fits Meigs' syndrome best.
